correctness.rationale: A chain of k triangles meeting at articulation vertices has 3^k recurrent states by the blockwise burning condition. The explicit maximal odometer U(v_i)=2i (i<k), U(v_k)=2k-1, U(w_i)=2i-1 satisfies reduced Laplacian L U=e_{v{k-1}}+e_{vk}+e_{wk}. Least action bounds every initial recurrent state, with equality precisely when the last two triangle blocks carry (1,1). This gives 3^(k-2) maximizers and stationary probability 1/9; the harmonic-potential solution gives E(total topplings)=(2k^2+k)/3. Independent direct stabilization over all 3^k codes for k=2,...,6 confirmed both the extremizer criterion and exact mean; finite evidence is not the all-k proof.

value.rationale: The effect of a fixed distal drive on a natural cactus family yields a non-obvious nonvanishing probability 1/9 of an O(k^2) extreme avalanche, with a two-block local recurrence certificate and an exact stationary mean. This is a structural stationary-law phenomenon, not a trivial sandpile group-order computation or tiny enumeration, and distinguishes maximal avalanches from typical-size scaling.

limitations: Only one-grain addition at the distal vertex, sink at root, uniform recurrent stationary measure and k>=2.
Full event law for all avalanche sizes is not asserted.
